scenes.headline: Databricks Workflows
scenes.subtitle: Orchestrate multi-step jobs with dependencies
scenes.narration: Databricks Workflows orchestrate multiple tasks into a dependency graph with scheduling, retries, and alerting.

scenes.headline: What Workflows provide
items: Tasks wired into a directed dependency graph
Mixed task types: notebooks, DLT, SQL, Python
scenes.narration: A workflow chains tasks so each runs after its dependencies complete. Tasks can be notebooks, DLT pipelines, SQL queries, or scripts in one job. Built-in scheduling, retries, and alerts keep pipelines running reliably.

scenes.headline: A multi-task job
scenes.narration: An ingestion task loads new data, then a transform task refines it. An aggregation task builds gold outputs once transformation succeeds. A final task sends a notification when the run completes.

scenes.headline: Workflows vs external orchestrators
scenes.narration: Workflows run natively with no separate orchestrator to maintain and give tight cost and lineage visibility. External tools like Airflow shine when coordinating many systems beyond Databricks. Many teams use Workflows for in-platform pipelines and an external tool for cross-system flows.

scenes.headline: Best practices
items: Use job clusters that spin up and terminate per run
Parameterize with widgets and job parameters
scenes.narration: Ephemeral job clusters isolate runs and control cost by shutting down afterward. Per-task retries and timeouts contain transient failures. Parameters make one workflow reusable across dates and environments.

scenes.text: Workflows turn a pile of tasks into a reliable, scheduled, observable pipeline.
scenes.narration: Define the dependencies once, and let the platform run them on time, every time.
